Subject: Initial: Order Form redlines — pricing schedule, min commits, invoicing

Ben — thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has reviewed the draft Order Form and we have a few commercial items to clarify before legal will sign: 

1) Pricing staircase — our FP&A wants the quarterly commit breakouts documented (year 1: 250k tokens/month, year 2: 500k tokens/month) and a clear uplift schedule. Can you confirm the final unit price for each tranche and whether usage above the commit will be billed at blended or on-demand rates?

2) Minimum commit & phasing — we need more flexibility on ramp. Can you accept a 6-month ramp (25% / 50% / 100%) rather than upfront annual minimum? If not, what alternatives do you suggest?

3) Net terms & invoicing — Acme pays on Net30, but the Order Form currently shows Net45. Also we need invoices routed to accounting@acme-corp.com and to the local EU entity (Acme EMEA) for tax/reclaim.

4) Taxes — our tax team asks about VAT handling and whether Redwood will issue invoices showing VAT separately or if we need to reverse-charge. We can provide EU VAT ID if needed.

Attached: draft OrderForm v2 with our comments (we'll re-upload final redline after your reply).

Goal: Can we get a coordinated commercial response today? Procurement is timeboxed on their approval window.

Thanks,
Tom Blake
Head of Procurement — Acme Corp

Tom — really appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front, then a proposed next step: 

- Pricing staircase: we can confirm tranche pricing but need to lock on token definition and measurement window (rolling 30d vs calendar month). If Acme prefers blended overage pricing we can offer a blended overage cap for committed tiers — I will include numbers in the attached redline.

- Min commit & phasing: we can support a 6-month ramp as a concession for this deal, provided the total annual committed spend still meets the quoted tier. I'll add explicit phasing language to the Order Form (25%/50%/100%) and include a catch-up/apportionment clause if usage falls short.

- Net terms & invoicing: finance prefers Net45 normally; that said, for strategic customers we can move to Net30 with a Sales credit schedule impact. Kimberly is cc'd to confirm operational implications (invoice cadence and PO handling).

- Taxes: we typically issue gross invoices with VAT shown if applicable; if Acme provides an EU VAT ID we'll include the reverse-charge notation on the invoice. Karthik, can Legal confirm the exact invoice language for EU reverse charge and entity-level invoicing?

Proposed next step: I attached a redline (OrderForm_ACME_v2_redline.docx) with: pricing table, explicit commit phasing, an invoice routing block to list two entities, and a Net30/Net45 option with a checkbox for Acme to select. If that looks good, we can send a DocuSign request and lock commercial terms in 24–48 hours.

Please review the attached and tell me if Acme will accept Net30 and the two-entity invoicing flow.

Thanks —

Ben / Tom — I reviewed the proposed redline. A few legal/ops notes we should align on before routing to signatures: 

1) Invoicing entity mapping: Redwood can support issuing invoices to multiple entities but needs a single payer clause ("Billing Entity") to limit accounting exposure. Proposed language: Acme will identify the Billing Entity for each invoice cycle; Redwood's acceptance of an invoice to an alternate entity is without waiver of Redwood's right to collect from the Billing Entity. This protects us if one local entity refuses payment.

2) VAT / Reverse charge: If Acme provides a valid VAT registration number for the invoiced entity, Redwood will include the reverse-charge reference and no VAT will be charged. For local withholding or non-EU taxes, we will follow the invoice law of the invoicing country. Please add a line for Acme to populate VAT IDs next to each entity in the Order Form.

3) Minimum commit ramp & catch-up: Agree with the phasing but add a 90-day catch-up window at the end of the ramp period to prevent permanent shortfalls. If catch-up is not achieved, the shortfall will be invoiced at the committed tranche price (not on-demand).

4) Net terms: We can accept Net30 commercially if Finance signs off on the credit exposure. Kimberly, please confirm any credit-control or pricing adjustments (e.g., prepayment discount removal) needed.

If Acme accepts the Billing Entity + VAT ID approach we'll prepare a narrow legal addendum so Sales can get signatures quickly. I can draft the clause and circulate.
